perspective-spread.quote: No panelist dissents on the core question — the vote is 3-0 against the gate. The remaining disagreement is only about emphasis and sequencing
perspective-spread.reason: It shows three panelist positions and keeps their sequencing differences visible: measure first, build council.yaml now, or instrument first. But all three are the same 'No' with different framing. The one real tension, the red-team gap for advisory units, is never weighed against the final verdict.

decision-clarity.quote: Do not add a mechanical dissent/agreement gate to `src/runner/execution/patterns/panel.mjs`.
decision-clarity.reason: The recommendation is clear and actionable. The revisit condition, 'if K2/K3 trip', relies on thresholds the deliverable never defines, and '~30 panel runs' is approximate.

counterfactual-depth.quote: panel units without a producer (advisory/discussion units) get no red-team coverage — the only acknowledged hole in the "enough" argument.
counterfactual-depth.reason: It names an alternative (an opt-in council workflow) and identifies a weakness in its own premise. It does not test that weakness, and it still concludes that red-team is 'sufficient', which contradicts the acknowledged hole.

evidence-discipline.quote: `reviewed.mjs:24-29, 52-54` — `high`/`critical` rigor and `code` capability already add a `red-team` checker
evidence-discipline.reason: Claims carry many file:line citations, which this judge cannot verify without the repo. The claim that item (4) 'needs no code change' merges genuineSplit with a confidence-weighted tally without support. The text does not mark what is inference and what is unverified.

execution-quality.quote: after ~30 panel runs, run `fgos metrics discussions --by workflow` ... if K2/K3 trip, build the council gates as an opt-in `core/workflows/council.yaml`
execution-quality.reason: The next step and its conditional follow-up are concrete. It names no owner and no deadline, and the only rollback is 'opt-in'.

perspective-spread.quote: the premise that "red-team already covers it" is only partly true.
perspective-spread.reason: It sets the question's two framings against each other (gate, or existing safeguards are enough) and rejects parts of both. Still, it is a single voice. No competing advocate's case is laid out and compared.

decision-clarity.quote: K2 fires: at least 90% of the first 30 logged panel runs are unanimous. K3 fires: a unanimous panel is later reversed by red-team or by a human within 14 days.
decision-clarity.reason: It gives a clear position with explicit numeric thresholds for reversing it, and it specifies what would be built if a threshold fires (opt-in, triggered by measured agreement).

counterfactual-depth.quote: A dissent quota would push models to produce disagreement while the actual weakness, correlated providers, stays in place.
counterfactual-depth.reason: It tests the strongest alternative against the real failure mode. It also shows that neither existing safeguard is guaranteed, citing the recorded Codex-only panel. And it states concrete conditions that would change the decision.

evidence-discipline.quote: The spec records a Codex-only panel that was "not cross-provider independent review" (runner.md:1404-1405).
evidence-discipline.reason: Key claims are tied to quoted spec text and line numbers, though their correctness is unverified. It flags one uncertainty, that the sensor may be collecting nothing. Most claims still lack explicit evidence or inference tags.

execution-quality.quote: If the count is near zero, the sensor isn't collecting anything. In that case, pass `--stance-options` in the panel workflows first, so K2 and K3 can be checked before K5 expires.
execution-quality.reason: The step is concrete, has a conditional branch and is time-bounded only by K5 expiry. It names no owner, no explicit deadline and no rollback criteria.

limits: I had no repository access, so every file:line citation in both deliverables (panel.mjs, reviewed.mjs, runner.md, observe.md) is unverified.
Neither deliverable defines K5, and A does not define K2/K3; I could not check them against the spec.
Both deliverables appear to exceed the 300-word limit, A by a wide margin. The rubric does not score length, so this did not change any score.
A is a multi-panelist synthesis and B is a single-voice position. The difference in format affects how perspective-spread can show up in each.
